turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How can I help you?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Hi, I just was brought in here today. I had a fall just waking up coming down the stairs. I fell off the last few stairs and just fell onto the right side and on, right onto my head and now, uh I couldn't even I could barely stand up and put any weight on my hip. It's the right hip.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, Uhm, so what caused you to fall in the 1st place? Did you just lose balance, were you dizzy?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think I just I missed, I wasn't dizzy or anything. I just missed one of the steps and just slipped, slipped down the stairs.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: But it was just the last few stairs I didn't have like I didn't hit my head or anything like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and when was this?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: This was a so I guess now two hours ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Two hours ago, OK. Has a pain been constant since?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, it's, it's really excruciating.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, does anything make it better or worse?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, it's I'm just in extreme pain. Like I I I can't even put any weight on it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so you can't, OK so you can't weight bear, and you can't walk on on that leg I guess.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Mhmm.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Is it a sharp kind of pain or is it dull and achy?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's uh, it's pretty sharp, like if I'm not putting any weight on it right now, it's like really achy. But if I put any weight on, it's really sharp.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And where is this pain exactly? Is it just in your right hip or is it radiating up into your upper anterior lower back or down to your leg?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's in the right hip, mostly just on the side, but the pain is kind of like, all over the right side of my groin and I feel like there's some swelling there as well.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And one to 10, 10 being the worst pain ever. How bad is your pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say 10, like I've never experienced pain like this.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: 10, OK. And do you, have you ever had pain like this before? Like have you ever had a fall in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, this isn't this is the first time I've had a fall.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any numbness or tingling?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, no, not that I can tell, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Dizziness or fainting spells?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, after the fall out like this, I I don't know if it's due to the pain, but even in the ambulance, coming out of the ambulance I was feeling a little bit dizzy, but I don't know if that's just 'cause of the pain.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any headaches?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Confusion or memory loss?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Uh, joint pains or muscle aches elsewhere?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Weight loss recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Fevers or chills?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Uhm, and rashes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any changes to your vision, hearing, smell or taste?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any, uh, you experiencing any cough, uhm, shortness of breath or wheezing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about chest pain or heart palpitations?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not that I have experienced.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how about changes your bowel movements?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about changes to urine?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And. Are you otherwise healthy? Do you have any longstanding medical conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, so I just have a, uhm I do have some osteoarthritis and then I have, I take this medication for blood pressure. It's called uh, Ramipril.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. OK, and is that the only medication that you're on?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, yeah. And then I'm just on vitamins like vitamin D, calcium and just multivitamins.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And are you up to date with your immunizations?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, OK. Any allergies?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, not that I know of.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Any family history of lung or heart conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, I think, uh my father, he died of a heart attack in his 60s.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK, any musculoskeletal issues?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, no, I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No. Uhm, how about autoimmune conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not that I know of.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any cancers?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, I think, my, my mother had some skin cancer, but the ones that, she didn't need any surgery, they just zapped them off.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Uhm and do you smoke?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I've never smoked?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, uhm, do you drink alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Just maybe like a wine, what every other day, a glass of of wine.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and then do you consume marijuana in any form?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And how about in terms of where you live? Who do you live with and where do you live?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I live with uhm, just my husband and and we just live in a small apartment.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And have you been in touch with any, anyone sick recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh. No, I've I've been like at home with my husband. We haven't really left.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And have you done any travel recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, no, I've just stayed at home.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Alright, so let's move on to the physical exam part of this interview. So if you can, I'm going to get you to take a look at both your hips as well as your legs. Do you notice any redness or swelling in the area?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I do notice some swelling. It's a little bit red. I can't really see too much red.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. OK. Any muscle atrophy? Any deformities or skin changes like bruises?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, maybe some bruising, but I, I don't notice anything else.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Alright. And then when you place the back of your hand on both hips, do you notice any temperature changes? Is one side warmer than the other?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's a little bit warmer, the right side than the left.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and does one like appear to be shorter? Or does does it appear to be misaligned? Or in any sort of like strange positions like outward turning of your leg, one compared to the other?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think it's a bit, but look at it a bit, like outward turning. And then yeah, I would say it's more outward turns.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and if are you sitting down right now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, are you able to stand up from a sitting position?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I can try, but it's very painful.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes, should I go ahead and try?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yes please.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah. So I yeah I can barely stand up. I can't, it's kind of just, I'm just supporting myself with my left like.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK and so I, I guess you can't do any of the like hip flexion or hip extension, hip abduction or addduction, correct?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I can barely move it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK alright those are all the questions that I had. Did you have any questions of your own?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I think I I just don't know if I need surgery or something.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, so it sounds like you have a hip fracture from your fall. Uhm, so, the way to treat this is a combination of surgeries and rehab and medication. So we will definitely look into the surgical option first, which is done using some internal repair with screws. Or, you can do a total hip replacement or a partial hip replacement. The orthopaedic surgeon will uh, decide like which option is best for you after we refer you for a consult with them, and then after that surgery they'll likely refer you to some rehab, so physiotherapy will focus on improving your range of motion and strengthening the muscles in that area. Uhm, and for management of pain, you can take ibuprofen or any over the counter pain medications for now. Does that sound OK?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, that sounds good. Thank you so much.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, great, no problem.
